statements.statement: New growth revenue for FY27 is about $1.4 million, split roughly $700,000 to schools and $700,000 to the town side/other departments.
Of the new revenue, $250,000 is being used for capital projects despite other funds that could have been used.
$180,000 of new revenue is going to the finance committee reserve account, though the policy figure is $50,000.
$80,000 of new revenue is going toward hiring a new town manager.
The listed town-side new-revenue allocations (capital, reserve, town manager hire, etc.) total $510,000 net.
The schools needed $761,000 to be at current level services and that funding was not provided.
The override would add about $800 a year to a taxpayer's bill, or about $650 depending on home value ($350,000-$480,000 range).
The board's letter urges increasing special education circuit breaker funding (line item 761-0012) to achieve 90% reimbursement.
The board's letter urges increasing Section 3 local aid distributions to at least $175 per pupil for minimum aid districts.
The Senate Ways and Means proposal includes a $53 million increase to unrestricted general government aid, bringing total UGGA funding to approximately $1.376 billion statewide.
